<reason>Both sides were strong, original, and epistemically clean, but B built the more durable path. B's central frame — the dial is never empty, so the motion reallocates control from engagement algorithms to parents rather than creating power — survived every round and was partially conceded by A ("she is not free today"). B's mechanism-vs-content distinction (disable the ranking engine, not decide which clinic page loads) shrank A's signature censorship claim from "censors of a developing mind" to a much weaker point about platforms classifying feeds, and A never recovered the original escalation. On the capability-becomes-duty slope, B's pressure question demanding a single real instance exposed that A's claim was conjecture; A's "this device is categorically different" answer was plausible but precedent-free, and B converted it into "two conjectures, no instance." A landed genuine counters — the lock rules the primary device even if workarounds exist, the captured non-bypassing population is exactly the vulnerable one, and confiscation is visible while an OS flag is quiet and portable — and these kept the debate competitive, but the best of them arrived as late crystallization rather than neutralizing B's fork. A also carried a small execution cost from the clipped Rebuttal 1. B answered both pressure questions directly with A1/A2 structure, narrowed the dispute each round, and closed on the cleanest weighing: certain nightly harm versus speculative, uninstanced ones.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2 (B4.1): the answer to A's Q1 — "no recommendation feed" targets a mechanism apps already implement (chronological/search modes), with parents setting thresholds as they already do for app-store age ratings — decoupled the motion from editorial censorship and forced A's core harm claim to shrink; paired with B's unanswered demand for one real instance of a parental tool hardening into a neglect duty, it left A's case resting on conjecture while B's rested on a conceded fact about who sets the dial today.</best_rebuttal>
